content: {"decision":"Reject current behavior: leases do not enforce a global limit of 4 when calls outlive them. Fail closed when capacity is uncertain.","risks":["Both controllers can allocate the same apparent capacity during Redis outages.","Expired leases can be repeatedly replaced while prior calls continue, causing unbounded concurrency.","Retries and controller restarts can duplicate calls or lose track of active work."],"required_changes":["Acquire permits atomically from one authoritative pool of 4; prohibit local fallback allocation and fail closed on uncertain acquisition or renewal.","Do not reclaim a permit merely because its lease expires. Retain uncertain occupancy until completion or confirmed termination; otherwise require generation-side enforcement that prevents replacement work from overlapping orphaned calls.","Use unique ownership tokens and conditional renewal/release so stale controllers cannot alter replacement permits. Fencing alone must not be treated as cancellation of running calls.","Bound queues, retries, and execution duration; make dispatch idempotent and reconcile active calls after recovery before reopening capacity."],"evidence_needed":["Fault tests covering simultaneous controller admission, Redis partitions/failover, lease expiry during long calls, delayed renewal/release, and controller crashes/restarts.","Generation-side start/end traces demonstrating actual concurrent calls never exceed 4 throughout faults and recovery.","Proof of atomic permit handling, stale-owner rejection, duplicate suppression, and any claimed cancellation or execution-time bound."]}
